key: What time hath past since they were first set flowing?
s: Opening a hymn chiefly to Indra, the verse tells of waters that never rest from flowing; Sāyaṇa, on 2.30.1, reads the question as rhetorical, the time of their first creation being no time at all, since the waters are eternal.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 2.30.1, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 213335 (2019)

opened.locator: 2.30.1 and its note on the drift of the question

evidence.words: आसां प्रथमः सर्गः प्राथमिकं जन्म कियात्या । कियति काले निष्पन्नं । आकारः प्रश्ने । किंशब्द आक्षेपे । यावति काले ता अजायंत स कालः कियान् । किं परिमाणं तस्य कालस्य । न किमपि । नित्या एव हि ता इत्यर्थः ।
evidence.gloss: Their first creation (sargaḥ), their first birth: in how long a time (kiyātyā) was it brought about? The ā marks a question; the word kim is used in dismissal. The time in which they were born, how long is it? What is the measure of that time? None at all. For they are eternal: that is the meaning.
evidence.licence: public domain text; transcription CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource)

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 2.30.1, at [220,1]); a single sentence ending in a question mark, which rule 8 allows. Opened the packet for 2.30.1: Sāyaṇa takes kim as ākṣepa (dismissal), asks the measure of the time of the waters’ first birth, answers na kim api, none at all, and concludes nityā eva hi tāḥ, they are eternal; Wilson’s note says the drift of the question according to the commentator is the eternity of the waters. ‘Rhetorical’ is a fair English for kim used in ākṣepa. Plain sense (waters that do not rest, opening the hymn to Indra) uses the first half of 2.30.1 without four words of the key sentence.
